thread:
mai: FYI support ticket from Acme — p95/p99 on /generate jumped around 10:22 UTC. They report p95 ~800ms, p99 up to 1.2s. No 5xxs, auth ok. Can SRE triage? :thinking:

alan: on it. any tenant-only pattern or global? model id? rate change?

bri: seeing an alert for gpux-3 pool at 10:21 for tail latency. Config rollout at 10:15 changed continuous-batcher behavior (enable adapt-grace).

zoe: grabbing logs now. quick check shows a lot of small batches (1-3 tokens) waiting ~30-60ms. grep snippet I ran:
```
kubectl logs -l app=batcher -n inference --since=30m | jq '.coalesce | {avg_wait_ms, p95_wait_ms, tail_batch_size: .tail_batches}' | head
```
sample: {"avg_wait_ms": 14, "p95_wait_ms": 78, "tail_batch_size": 1}

alan: repro steps I used locally:
1) spawn 200rps of tiny prompts ("hi")
2) set X-Tenant: acme and target /v1/generate
3) observe p95/p99 climb after ~2m
command: ```bash
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -H "X-Tenant: acme" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":8}' $ENDPOINT & done
```

bri: digging config diff — adapt-grace flips grace_window_ms from 6 -> 40 for low-throughput flows, and increases max_hold_ms threshold. For bursty short prompts that actually increases head-of-line blocking: many tiny requests wait until they coalesce into one bigger batch, but if one request in front takes long (KV/cache warmup), the whole batch tail spikes.

mai: Acme is short-prompt-heavy, high burstiness. Support has customers on free tier but this one is paid — they need SLA-level latency. Can we do a quick mitigation?

zoe: Options: 1) per-tenant override gracefully set acme.grace_window_ms=6 on gpux-3; 2) rollback adapt-grace cluster-wide; 3) route acme to low-latency pool with prefer-latency-mode enabled. Quick hotpatch below would be #1. Tradeoff: higher per-token cost.

alan: I can apply per-tenant override. Will patch configmap for gpux-3: 
```yaml
batcher:
  tenants:
    acme:
      grace_window_ms: 6
```
then roll config to batcher pods. Will monitor.

deploy-bot: @alan initiated config rollout to batcher/gpux-3 at 10:38 UTC — rollout id r-2026-10. Applying 3/3 pods.

alan: Hotpatch applied, acme.grace_window_ms=6, pods restarted one-by-one. Watching metrics.

bri: Observability — within 90s p95 dropped from ~820ms to ~160ms, p99 down to ~220ms. Snapshots: 
- before: p95 820ms, p99 1160ms
- after: p95 160ms, p99 220ms
(verified on gpux-3, tenant=acme)

mai: Customer confirmed latency returned to normal. I'll update ticket and recommend we keep per-tenant override while we evaluate. :white_check_mark:

zoe: Follow ups: add a short-prompt burst canary test to our perf suite, document per-tenant grace config in runbook, and add a dashboard to track grace_window changes vs p99. Also let's add a safety gate in rollout pipelines when adapt-grace toggles.

alan: filing a quick post-mortem task: SRE-5482 (investigate adapt-grace algorithm edge-cases for tiny bursts). Also will draft a short runbook entry for emergency per-tenant hotpatch.

mai: thanks team. closing loop with Acme and ops.

zoe: note: this one wasn't an auth/billing issue — just config tradeoff with continuous batching. Leaving a pinned snippet in the ticket with the repro steps and commands. :memo:
